full_judgment:
Respondent No.1 as the plaintiff instituted Mortgage Suit No.68 of 1978' in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong for redemption of 1.25 acres of lands described in schedules 1 and 2 to the plaint. His case, in short, is that the disputed property described in the schedule to the plaint belonged to late Prasanna Kumar Dutta father of the plaintiff and proforma defendants by purchase and exchange. The father of the plaintiff mortgaged the disputed property to defendant Nos.1, 2, and 3 and father of defendant Nos.4-6 for Tk.6000 (six thousand) by a mortgage deed dated 25-11-1962 registered on 13-12-1962 and delivered the possession of the mortgaged land to the mortgagee that with a view to avoiding legal complications. The deed was executed as a deed of sale but from the long period of 10 years mentioned in the deed as well as from the subsequent conducts of the parties, it would clearly appear that the intention of the parties was to make it a mortgage by conditional sale. The mortgage was to be redeemed within 10 years. The mortgagees enjoyed the mortgaged properties for over 15 years for the principal amount and maximum interest available to the mortgagees thereon. Anukul Dutta and Natun Dutta were co-sharers in the khatian of the mortgaged land. Kuntala Dutta, daughter of Anukul Dutta, instituted Partition Suit No.39 of 1964 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong for partition of the suit land along with other ejmali land. The said partition suit was disposed of on 10.8.1968 on the basis of a solenama, which was made part of the decree. In the sole decree, it was provided that the suit land being in mortgage by conditional sale would be partitioned after redemption and after redemption, the heirs of Prasanna Kumar (the plaintiff and defendant Nos.7 to 13 of the said partition suit) would get 1/3rd share in the present suit land. The plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.178· of 1972-73 in the Court of the then Sub-Divisional Officer, Chittagong for redemption of the suit land. The Sub-Divisional Officer by his order dated 21-2-1974 allowed the redemption and directed the defendants (appellants herein) under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to restore possession to the plaintiff by 10-3- 1974. Meanwhile, the High Court Division declared the relevant law as illegal and void and, as such, the plaintiff has subsequently instituted the present suit for the reliefs as stated above in the plaint. The defendants in Pre-emption Case No.106 of 1973 in the Court of Munsif, First Court, Chittagong, admitted that the suit land is mortgaged property. 

 10. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, submits that according to section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the transaction is a complete usufructuary mortgage as the right of repurchase. was up to 25-11-1972 and President's Order No.88 of 1972 came into effect on 3-8-1972 and, as such, no interference is called for. 

 14. Sub-sections 4 and 5 of section 95 and section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act were introduced by President's Order No.88 of 1972 on 30-8-1972. 

 15. Initially the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No. 178/72-73 in the Court of the then Sub- divisional Officer, Chittagong for redemption of the suit land and the then Sub-divisional Officer by his order dated 21-2-1974 allowed redemption and directed the defendants under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to restore the possession of the suit land to the plaintiff on 10-3-1974. Meanwhile, the High Court Division declared the relevant law illegal and void and, as such, the plaintiff subsequently instituted the suit for the reliefs as stated in the plaint. In the case of Bangladesh vs Haji Abdul Gani Biswas, (1980) 32 DLR (AD) 233, the Appellate Division found that President's Order Nos.88 and 136 of 1974 and 24 of 1973 were valid legislation affecting necessary amendments in the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and those laws cannot be attacked on the ground of ultra vires. The Appellate Division further held as under: 

 17. In this connection, it is also pertinent to quote section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as under: 

 "95A. Treatment of certain transaction as usufructuary mortgage-Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972] (President's Order No.88 of 1972)." 

 18. Having considered section 95A and the principle laid down in the case of Bangladesh vs Haji Abdul Gani Biswas (ibid), it appears that the sale of the present case having been made on 25-11-1962 with the condition of repurchase within 10 years from the date of the deed of sale and the condition giving right of repurchase having survived till introduction of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, vide, President's Order No.88 of 1972 had become a complete usufructuary mortgage and the period of redemption is 60 years. 

 21. In the case in hand, the plaintiff's father sold the suit property on 25-5-1962 with a condition of repurchase within 10 years, i.e. till 24-11-1972 and President's Order No..88 of 1972 came into effect on 3-8-1972 and the condition giving right of repurchase survived when President's Order No.88 of 1972 came into effect and, as such, the sale in the present case had become a complete usufructuary mortgage within the meaning of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Therefore, the case of Somedullah (ibid) has no manner of application on the facts and in, the circumstances of the present case.
